title: AWS US-EAST-1 Kinesis Overload and Cascading Failure
summary: A capacity management error in AWS US-EAST-1 caused Amazon Kinesis to become overloaded, triggering a cascading failure across multiple dependent AWS services including Cognito, CloudWatch, and Lambda. The incident lasted approximately seven hours and affected a large number of customers.
impact: Widespread degradation of AWS services in the US-EAST-1 region for approximately 7 hours. Services affected included Amazon Kinesis, AWS Lambda, Amazon Cognito, Amazon CloudWatch, AWS EventBridge, and others relying on internal control planes.

timeline.description: Automated activity triggered a capacity management error causing front-end server overload in the Kinesis data plane.
AWS engineers identify the root cause and begin scaling the Kinesis front-end fleet.
Kinesis and most dependent services recover to full operation.

causal_factors.description: An automated capacity management activity added capacity in a way that overloaded the front-end Kinesis servers beyond their thread limits.
Multiple internal AWS services used Kinesis as a control plane channel, causing cascading errors when Kinesis degraded.

lessons.statement: Hidden internal dependencies on shared infrastructure should be explicitly tracked and visible in service maps.
lessons.recommended_control: Maintain a live service dependency graph and run regular dependency audits on critical infrastructure.

lessons.statement: Services recovering from a dependency outage should use exponential backoff with jitter to prevent thundering herd re-triggers.
lessons.recommended_control: Review retry and reconnect logic across all services that depend on shared control-plane infrastructure.
